title: Role sync orchestration and customer migration notice for RBAC v2 rollout
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Orchestrate a staged role synchronization and customer notification program to move accounts from the legacy RBAC v1 model to RBAC v2. Deliverables include a reversible migration harness (shadow sync + progressive promotion), enhanced audit alignment between auth events and the new role ledger, SAML/SSO attribute mapping verification, admin console safeguards, and a customer-facing migration timeline and opt-in instructions.
acceptance_criteria: Shadow sync completes for 100% of internal teams with zero permission regressions in canary samples
Audit events schema documented and ingested into ELK/Kinesis for both v1 and v2 during transition window
SAML attribute map validated against 10 representative enterprise IdPs and automated mapping tests added to CI
Canary group promotion path automated with timeboxed rollback and observable metrics for errors and permission denies
Customer comms (email + console banner + knowledge base) drafted, reviewed by legal, sent to pilot customers 7 days before visible promotion
tasks: Design shadow role sync: implement one-way replication from v1->v2 in dry-run mode
Build reconciliation job that computes permission diffs and emits deterministic reconciliation reports
Add delta telemetry: permission mismatch rate, rejected mappings, SSO attribute failures
Create admin 'promotion' flow with explicit confirmation, dry-run preview, and rate limits
Author customer migration playbook and email templates; partner with solutions to schedule pilot migrations
Create migration dashboard (per-customer) showing sync status, last recon, and open issues
Add automated test matrix for SAML mappings across common IdPs (Okta, Azure AD, PingFederate)
Wire audit pipeline: tag events with migration-phase and role-version for downstream retention

risk_mitigation: Keep shadow sync read-only by default; only enable promotion via opt-in flag per-customer
Limit concurrent promotions to 10 customers/hour and queue with backoff to avoid load spikes
Maintain v1 authorization path for 14 days after promotion with synchronized audit tagging for forensics
Pre-flight tests: permission smoke tests and end-to-end SSO login verification for each pilot account
Emergency rollback: revoke promotion flag and trigger automated reconciliation to restore v1-anchored permissions
rollback_plan: If any canary exhibits >0.1% unexpected permission denial or a spike in 5xx auth errors, immediately pause promotions, run automated reconciliation to restore v1 representation, notify impacted customers via the migration dashboard and support channel, and create a postmortem. Rollback steps are scripted in the runbook and tested in staging.
notes: Prefer metrics that are deterministic and auditable (hash of role assignments) to reduce false positives in reconciliation
Consider adding a 'visibility-only' toggle for admins so customers can preview how RBAC v2 would map before promoting
Coordinate with Console team to add migration banners that link to per-customer status pages
Discuss longer retention of migration-phase audit logs with Compliance for regulated customers
